# Sahana System Limited: growth, claims and cash do not yet reconcile

## 1. Executive Verdict

**Hold — unresolved; research priority, not an investment endorsement.** Sahana is an Ahmedabad-based IT services and systems-integration group expanding into defence electronics, digital infrastructure and EV-related assets. Reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹331.15cr and operating profit growth are substantial, and verified government-channel opportunities are commercially relevant. The decisive obstacle is not SME status or a high growth rate: it is the inability to reconcile material promoter-related debt, owner earnings per share and cash-flow classifications, alongside recurring control-report limitations and overdue statutory dues. At the verified 19 October 2026 close of ₹962.85, ordinary headline multiples are not enough to establish an attractive setup. BQS, GQS and IAS remain **NS**, rather than invented low or neutral ratings. This is an acquisition-led emerging technology/infrastructure **special-situation research thesis**, not an evidence-backed compounder. A signed financial reconciliation, actual collection/claim-settlement evidence and a constant-perimeter growth/capital bridge would change the evidence assessment. A lower price alone would not clear these gates. [E02–E12]

No fabricated October TTM.

## 4. Business Overview

The historical core is software development, systems integration, implementation, digital transformation and enterprise/government IT projects. Hardware and software are increasingly delivered together. The customer buys execution, integration and service support, not necessarily proprietary software with subscription economics. Cash collection can lag project recognition, and advances/deposits can precede customer billing. Contract-specific acceptance, warranty, maintenance and principal-versus-agent economics are not fully disclosed, so revenue is not equated with recurring software ARR. [AR26 PDF70,129,150; E09]

FY26 group revenue comprises **₹242.98cr services**, **₹86.17cr goods**, and **₹2cr unbilled revenue** in note23. Standalone goods revenue is **₹101.16cr**, versus ₹7.83cr the year before, and constitutes **42.76%** of standalone sales. Group goods are lower than standalone goods, consistent with the need for an elimination/classification bridge, but the exact bridge was not located. Do not combine standalone hardware with group services. The narrative that the company is moving away from low-margin hardware is therefore not a sufficient explanation of the disclosed mix. Gross profit/value added, geographic contribution, recurring revenue, retention and customer-level margins remain ND. [AR26 PDF70,150]

Softvan and Softvan Labs were acquired in August 2023; Softvan's subsequent evolution into Sahana Defence materially changes the group. FY26 economic interests include Sahana Defence **76.37%**, Softvan Labs 100%, Sourceved 51%, Applie 51%, Futurio 60%, Techanalysis 60%, Marine 75%, Health 80% and the US subsidiary 100%. These are not nine interchangeable wholly owned cash pools. Subsidiary cash may not be legally or economically available to discharge the parent's obligations, and non-controlling interests matter in valuation. The reported segment aggregation does not supply a sufficient sum-of-parts earnings/capital allocation. [AR26 PDF58–60,157–160; E08–E14]

## 5. Moat / Industry Position

**Mechanism → evidence → durability → failure mode:**

1. Integration know-how and delivery relationships can reduce implementation risk. The government-channel projects and expanding service sales show commercial access. But there is no measured retention, switching cost, price premium, win-rate history or proprietary platform profitability. A capable systems integrator can compete through tenders, vendor partnerships and delivery teams; time/cost to replicate are ND. This supports useful but contestable capabilities, not a structural monopoly.
2. Defence qualification and a CEL operating arrangement could become a barrier. The June 2026 contract is evidence of access, not completed qualification, fully funded capacity, contracted purchase volumes or earned high-margin defence revenue. The failure mode is spending before qualification and production demand.
3. Existing customer concentration may create reference value, but also dependence. FY24 top-ten customers were **89.08%** of revenue, versus 82% FY23 and 91.46% FY22. These are dated figures, not current concentration. Current top customers, supplier concentration, connected-party screening and renewal/termination terms remain gaps. [AR24 PDF61; IPO customer section]

Three named primary economic peers are included, not selected merely for small capitalization. FY26 reported revenue/strict operating EBIT/CFO are approximately **Dev IT ₹189.50cr/−₹0.03cr/−₹2.14cr**, **Silver Touch ₹341.99cr/₹51.34cr/₹17.15cr**, and **Dynacons ₹1,424.28cr/₹131.40cr/₹46.13cr**. ## 7. Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway

There are identifiable avenues, but not a quantified, proven accessible TAM. The July RailTel **₹69.51cr IGAS PLOI** concerns Deendayal Port, Kandla, includes GST and five-year O&M, and remains conditional on approvals/formal order. The separate **₹2.54cr** website/CMS-related PLOI also includes GST. They must not be added as fully executable backlog, immediately recognized sales or recurring high-margin service revenue. Opening backlog plus intake less execution/cancellation cannot be reconciled from the disclosed material. [RAIL31; RAIL11]

Sahana Defence's **10-year CEL facility contract**, extendible by five years subject to performance, provides a route into electronic warfare/weapon peripheral activity. Minimum offtake, customer qualification timing, incremental capex, working-capital intensity and margins were not verified. The October SPA for **60% of Siddhanta Machining** adds a potential manufacturing capability but remains conditional on completion and a valuation/diligence-adjusted price. Target FY25 revenue was only ₹0.8477cr, below FY23 ₹3.4785cr. Target promoter/director Yogesh Vinodkumar Pajni also joined Sahana Defence's board in May 2026, making the related-party context important. Management says arm's-length independent valuation; the underlying valuation was not located. No acquired revenue or zero-cost assumption is treated as established. If ownership is unchanged, 76.37%×60%=45.822% ultimate economic exposure is arithmetic, not a finalized closing structure. [CEL15; AGREE01]

The growth experiment therefore starts from verified sales, then separately assumes growth, EBITDA margin, receivable days, inventory/advance ratios and investment. It is not a bottom-up customer/capacity forecast, because counts, utilization and unit margins are absent. The missing bottom-up proof is explicitly the reason REV/CAP remain NS. FY26 **₹36.00cr CWIP** includes NMW dashboard ₹14.90cr, generic CWIP ₹15cr and Sahana House ₹6.10cr. EV ₹7.41cr and GIS ₹9.485cr moved out of CWIP into assets, which documents capitalization, not commercially proven cash returns. [AR26 PDF141–143]

Growth ≈ reinvestment rate×incremental return is used only as a terminal consistency check. Terminal reinvestment is at least NOPAT×g/ROIC and at least the capital stock required to sustain g. This prevents free growth in the final year. The GQS cap is due to recurring weak cash realization, not because cash capex was mistakenly subtracted from CFO.

## 11. Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path

The central thesis-break variable is **collectible operating cash after honoring actual senior/statutory claims**, not a reported sales growth rate. Customer acceptance delays or loss of a concentrated contract can combine with hardware purchase commitments, advanced project spending and qualification delays. Margins fall, receivables age, customer advances cease growing and cash leaves before collections. Statutory settlement and uncertain related-party claims then compress liquidity; uncommitted warrants may not convert, and external equity can dilute surviving owners. Asset goodwill, software and partially completed projects may not provide realizable recovery at book value. This is an economically coherent permanent-loss path, not a price-volatility story.

The strongest contrary evidence is real reported service expansion, FY26 positive operating cash, unmodified financial opinions, no reported bank default and comparatively modest stated bank borrowings. If debt discrepancies are disclosure errors and receivables/advances are recovered, the group's actual flexibility may be better than the stress tests suggest. Conversely, treating all apparent cash as unrestricted and all orders as revenue would overstate resilience. Permanent-impairment concern is **High**, but exact recovery/downside is NS while claim priority/recoverability are unknown. Hypothetical gaps quantify assumptions, not a finding that the company actually defaulted in the past or will default.

No differentiated market-mispricing claim is made: the market may already recognize these risks. Clearing G2 requires evidence, not assurances or a rally. [E04–E22]

Primary record set: FY23 directors report; FY24, FY25 and FY26 original annual reports; May2026 audited results and November2025 interim results; SEBI IPO prospectus/restated statements; October2024 rights letter; corporate-action and warrant notices; use-of-proceeds report; current NSE security master and60 exact NSE session bhavcopies; three peer audited annual reports. Sources are linked with exact SHA256, physical PDF pages and qualifications in **source_map.md, sources.json, audit_closure.json and market_peer_sources.json**. Source-safe archives contain authored extracts, not raw PDFs/OCR/full exchange datasets.

Key open questions are not cosmetic: (1) Which actual entity owes the promoter balances, with what repayment rights? (2) Why do group/standalone audit-trail and CARO descriptions differ? (3) Which cash-flow comparative changes are classifications versus errors? (4) What is corrected owner diluted EPS? (5) Which deposits/loans/advances are liquid, pledged or related, and can subsidiaries upstream cash? (6) What exact CCD/bonus-adjusted warrant claims apply? (7) How much growth and capital is organic? (8) What is Siddhanta's binding price/closing status and project-level return evidence? Answers may improve or worsen the result; no predetermined misconduct conclusion is sought.

Model assumptions are in model_inputs.json, model_spec.md and every canonical path. **98 complete paths**, including **59 failed paths**, are retained. Historical and valuation calculations are rebuilt from declared authored inputs with no network/source dependency. Sixteen framework checks are addressed, with unresolved evidence shown rather than claiming every issuer question is closed. Standalone audit scope is never silently generalized to all subsidiaries, and a management forecast in an exchange filing remains a management forecast.

sections.title: Executive Verdict
sections.content_markdown: **Hold — unresolved; research priority, not an investment endorsement.** Sahana is an Ahmedabad-based IT services and systems-integration group expanding into defence electronics, digital infrastructure and EV-related assets. Reported FY26 consolidated revenue of ₹331.15cr and operating profit growth are substantial, and verified government-channel opportunities are commercially relevant. The decisive obstacle is not SME status or a high growth rate: it is the inability to reconcile material promoter-related debt, owner earnings per share and cash-flow classifications, alongside recurring control-report limitations and overdue statutory dues. At the verified 19 October 2026 close of ₹962.85, ordinary headline multiples are not enough to establish an attractive setup. BQS, GQS and IAS remain **NS**, rather than invented low or neutral ratings. This is an acquisition-led emerging technology/infrastructure **special-situation research thesis**, not an evidence-backed compounder. A signed financial reconciliation, actual collection/claim-settlement evidence and a constant-perimeter growth/capital bridge would change the evidence assessment. A lower price alone would not clear these gates. [E02–E12]

sections.title: Business Overview
sections.content_markdown:
The historical core is software development, systems integration, implementation, digital transformation and enterprise/government IT projects. Hardware and software are increasingly delivered together. The customer buys execution, integration and service support, not necessarily proprietary software with subscription economics. Cash collection can lag project recognition, and advances/deposits can precede customer billing. Contract-specific acceptance, warranty, maintenance and principal-versus-agent economics are not fully disclosed, so revenue is not equated with recurring software ARR. [AR26 PDF70,129,150; E09]

FY26 group revenue comprises **₹242.98cr services**, **₹86.17cr goods**, and **₹2cr unbilled revenue** in note23. Standalone goods revenue is **₹101.16cr**, versus ₹7.83cr the year before, and constitutes **42.76%** of standalone sales. Group goods are lower than standalone goods, consistent with the need for an elimination/classification bridge, but the exact bridge was not located. Do not combine standalone hardware with group services. The narrative that the company is moving away from low-margin hardware is therefore not a sufficient explanation of the disclosed mix. Gross profit/value added, geographic contribution, recurring revenue, retention and customer-level margins remain ND. [AR26 PDF70,150]

Softvan and Softvan Labs were acquired in August 2023; Softvan's subsequent evolution into Sahana Defence materially changes the group. FY26 economic interests include Sahana Defence **76.37%**, Softvan Labs 100%, Sourceved 51%, Applie 51%, Futurio 60%, Techanalysis 60%, Marine 75%, Health 80% and the US subsidiary 100%. These are not nine interchangeable wholly owned cash pools. Subsidiary cash may not be legally or economically available to discharge the parent's obligations, and non-controlling interests matter in valuation. The reported segment aggregation does not supply a sufficient sum-of-parts earnings/capital allocation. [AR26 PDF58–60,157–160; E08–E14]

sections.title: Moat / Industry Position
sections.content_markdown:
**Mechanism → evidence → durability → failure mode:**

1. Integration know-how and delivery relationships can reduce implementation risk. The government-channel projects and expanding service sales show commercial access. But there is no measured retention, switching cost, price premium, win-rate history or proprietary platform profitability. A capable systems integrator can compete through tenders, vendor partnerships and delivery teams; time/cost to replicate are ND. This supports useful but contestable capabilities, not a structural monopoly.
2. Defence qualification and a CEL operating arrangement could become a barrier. The June 2026 contract is evidence of access, not completed qualification, fully funded capacity, contracted purchase volumes or earned high-margin defence revenue. The failure mode is spending before qualification and production demand.
3. Existing customer concentration may create reference value, but also dependence. FY24 top-ten customers were **89.08%** of revenue, versus 82% FY23 and 91.46% FY22. These are dated figures, not current concentration. Current top customers, supplier concentration, connected-party screening and renewal/termination terms remain gaps. [AR24 PDF61; IPO customer section]

Three named primary economic peers are included, not selected merely for small capitalization. FY26 reported revenue/strict operating EBIT/CFO are approximately **Dev IT ₹189.50cr/−₹0.03cr/−₹2.14cr**, **Silver Touch ₹341.99cr/₹51.34cr/₹17.15cr**, and **Dynacons ₹1,424.28cr/₹131.40cr/₹46.13cr**. These audited records illustrate very different software/hardware and cash economics. Dev IT's exceptional ₹93.55cr fair-value gain makes headline PAT a poor operating comparison. Dynacons has material pledged cash and margins/deposits; do not net them all against debt. No unverified current peer P/E or market-share figure is used. Full consistent FY25/FY26 metrics, owner/group PAT, leases and formulas are in peer_inputs.json. [E17]

### Dev Information Technology Limited
IT services, digital transformation, managed infrastructure, e-governance and enterprise applications compete for comparable project budgets and skilled delivery resources. Service-led domestic and international mix, Microsoft Dynamics ecosystem through Dhyey, and investment remeasurement exposure. It is not a clean comparable for defence hardware, EV infrastructure or data-centre ownership.

A weaker operating/earnings-quality comparator: reported PAT is dominated by associate-investment reclassification gains, while core operating EBIT and CFO are weak. Do not transplant its headline P/E. Cash equivalents exclude investment holdings. FY26₹47.9782 cr investments are not operating cash. FY25₹11.6362 cr gain on sale of investment is inside other income; FY26₹93.5464 cr fair-value gain is exceptional and non-cash. Sources: PEER_DEV26; PDF locators {'P&L': '213', 'balance_sheet': '212', 'CFO': '214–215', 'exceptional': '244 note 34', 'other_income': '241–242 note 27'}.

### Silver Touch Technologies Limited
Government e-governance, system integration, software development and enterprise digital transformation closely overlap the project/customer economics of Sahana’s technology arm. A mature service/employee-intensive integrator with consolidated overseas entities and joint ventures. Hardware/stock purchases are smaller relative to revenue than Dynacons; not a pure Saa S recurring-revenue or defence-manufacturing peer.

Useful operating-margin comparator, but weak two-year cash conversion cautions against equating government-project PAT with distributable cash. ₹8.4082 cr other bank deposits have maturity>90 days; availability is not established, so they are not netted as unrestricted cash. Lease liabilities are hidden under other noncurrent/current liabilities and separately added. Sources: PEER_SILVER26; PDF locators {'P&L': '178', 'balance_sheet': '177', 'CFO': '182', 'cash': '198 notes 8–9', 'leases': '218'}.

### Dynacons Systems & Solutions Limited
BFSI/public-sector/enterprise digital infrastructure, turnkey systems integration, data centres, cloud and managed services provide a direct commercial/execution comparator. Much larger hardware/procurement/pass-through component and long-duration leasing/service commitments. Supplier financing, bank guarantees and restricted deposits matter; revenue multiples cannot be transferred mechanically to Sahana.

Stronger scale and delivery-history comparator, not a flawless cash benchmark: FY26 receivables grew faster than sales, and CFO fell while PAT rose. Of FY26₹12.8819 cr reported cash equivalents,₹12.33 cr deposits are pledged; only ₹0.5519 cr is a narrow unrestricted proxy. Additional ₹98.6315 cr bank margin money is restricted. sections.title: Growth Quality & Reinvestment Runway
sections.content_markdown:
There are identifiable avenues, but not a quantified, proven accessible TAM. The July RailTel **₹69.51cr IGAS PLOI** concerns Deendayal Port, Kandla, includes GST and five-year O&M, and remains conditional on approvals/formal order. The separate **₹2.54cr** website/CMS-related PLOI also includes GST. They must not be added as fully executable backlog, immediately recognized sales or recurring high-margin service revenue. Opening backlog plus intake less execution/cancellation cannot be reconciled from the disclosed material. [RAIL31; RAIL11]

Sahana Defence's **10-year CEL facility contract**, extendible by five years subject to performance, provides a route into electronic warfare/weapon peripheral activity. Minimum offtake, customer qualification timing, incremental capex, working-capital intensity and margins were not verified. The October SPA for **60% of Siddhanta Machining** adds a potential manufacturing capability but remains conditional on completion and a valuation/diligence-adjusted price. Target FY25 revenue was only ₹0.8477cr, below FY23 ₹3.4785cr. Target promoter/director Yogesh Vinodkumar Pajni also joined Sahana Defence's board in May 2026, making the related-party context important. Management says arm's-length independent valuation; the underlying valuation was not located. No acquired revenue or zero-cost assumption is treated as established. If ownership is unchanged, 76.37%×60%=45.822% ultimate economic exposure is arithmetic, not a finalized closing structure. [CEL15; AGREE01]

The growth experiment therefore starts from verified sales, then separately assumes growth, EBITDA margin, receivable days, inventory/advance ratios and investment. It is not a bottom-up customer/capacity forecast, because counts, utilization and unit margins are absent. The missing bottom-up proof is explicitly the reason REV/CAP remain NS. FY26 **₹36.00cr CWIP** includes NMW dashboard ₹14.90cr, generic CWIP ₹15cr and Sahana House ₹6.10cr. EV ₹7.41cr and GIS ₹9.485cr moved out of CWIP into assets, which documents capitalization, not commercially proven cash returns. [AR26 PDF141–143]

Growth ≈ reinvestment rate×incremental return is used only as a terminal consistency check. Terminal reinvestment is at least NOPAT×g/ROIC and at least the capital stock required to sustain g. This prevents free growth in the final year. The GQS cap is due to recurring weak cash realization, not because cash capex was mistakenly subtracted from CFO.

sections.content_markdown:
Pratik Ramjibhai Kakadia is chairman/managing director in the FY26 accounts. FY26 disclosed remuneration **₹0.8491cr** is about 1.25% of owner PAT; this alone neither proves alignment nor abuse. The much more important issue is capital and related-party exposure. The October notice reports promoter holding **57.31%** (6,077,021 shares) and non-promoter 42.69%; non-promoter shares are only an upper bound for freely tradable float. Cutoff encumbrance history was not fully established; do not call pledges zero merely because a field was not found. [AR26 PDF157; security_inputs.json]

**Original audit findings, not an aggregator summary:**

- Standalone FY26 audit says privileged/admin-user changes in the accounting software did not have the audit-trail feature enabled; retention is described only where enabled. No tampering is identified. Consolidated report says audit trail operated throughout and no adverse CARO reporting, so the parent/control context cannot be discarded. [AR26 PDF81–82,125]
- CARO lists undisputed income tax **₹656.09 lakh** and TDS **₹504.70 lakh** outstanding beyond six months at 31 March. These are statutory arrears as of that date, not a verified October balance. Tax settlement and interest/penalties after March are ND. **CARO explicitly reports no lender principal/interest default and no willful-defaulter declaration.** [AR26 PDF85]
- Internal audit reports could not be obtained/considered in FY25 and FY26 CARO, despite management's more favorable descriptions. The system existed; the issue is availability/reliance, not proof no internal audit occurred. [AR25 PDF100; AR26 PDF86]
- Consolidated opinion is unmodified; IFC opinion is favorable; no fraud noticed/reported is stated. These are meaningful counterfacts, not a clean bill cancelling contradictory notes. [AR26 PDF121,126–127]
- Original auditor Rahul Mistri's August 2023 resignation cited preoccupation. A.K. Ostwal filled the vacancy and subsequently received a term. No source establishes a resignation over scope denial. IPO restatement separately disclosed depreciation/tax/opening adjustments and cannot fairly be labelled an unexplained manipulation. The consolidated RPT note reports promoter loan taken **₹65.7819cr**, repaid **₹10.5599cr**, closing **₹54.2220cr**. The flows net to ₹55.2220cr, a further ₹1cr mismatch. Closing promoter balance is larger than total reported group borrowings **₹17.9323cr**, and note17 related-party demand debt is **₹1.5552cr**. sections.title: Bear Case & Permanent-Loss Path
sections.content_markdown:
The central thesis-break variable is **collectible operating cash after honoring actual senior/statutory claims**, not a reported sales growth rate. Customer acceptance delays or loss of a concentrated contract can combine with hardware purchase commitments, advanced project spending and qualification delays. Margins fall, receivables age, customer advances cease growing and cash leaves before collections. Statutory settlement and uncertain related-party claims then compress liquidity; uncommitted warrants may not convert, and external equity can dilute surviving owners. Asset goodwill, software and partially completed projects may not provide realizable recovery at book value. This is an economically coherent permanent-loss path, not a price-volatility story.

The strongest contrary evidence is real reported service expansion, FY26 positive operating cash, unmodified financial opinions, no reported bank default and comparatively modest stated bank borrowings. If debt discrepancies are disclosure errors and receivables/advances are recovered, the group's actual flexibility may be better than the stress tests suggest. Conversely, treating all apparent cash as unrestricted and all orders as revenue would overstate resilience. Permanent-impairment concern is **High**, but exact recovery/downside is NS while claim priority/recoverability are unknown. Hypothetical gaps quantify assumptions, not a finding that the company actually defaulted in the past or will default.

No differentiated market-mispricing claim is made: the market may already recognize these risks. Clearing G2 requires evidence, not assurances or a rally. [E04–E22]

sections.title: Final Classification & Conditional Action
sections.content_markdown:
**Hold — unresolved / Pending evidence.** All three composites are NS and no numeric ranking is appropriate. The raw mathematical bounds and GQS cap organize uncertainty; they are not a low-score placement. The evidence-backed compounder test is not met because critical factors, capital returns and cash resilience are unsupported, and gates are unresolved. No favorable action category follows from the apparent15× owner-PAT multiple.

The practical next step is **research priority**: obtain a reconciled promoter/group debt schedule, corrected owner-EPS and comparative cash-flow notes, statutory settlement/lien/fungibility evidence, and a constant-perimeter growth/capital bridge. If these resolve favorably, re-evaluate quality and rerun valuation using actual financing/operating terms and then-current market data. A lower price can improve conditional return, but cannot fix unreliable claims. No holdings, weights, taxes or cost bases were supplied, so no personalized exit count, allocation or trade is invented. No Git/site publication or trades are part of this dossier.

Source-safe archives contain authored extracts, not raw PDFs/OCR/full exchange datasets.

Key open questions are not cosmetic: (1) Which actual entity owes the promoter balances, with what repayment rights? (2) Why do group/standalone audit-trail and CARO descriptions differ? (3) Which cash-flow comparative changes are classifications versus errors? (4) What is corrected owner diluted EPS? (5) Which deposits/loans/advances are liquid, pledged or related, and can subsidiaries upstream cash? (6) What exact CCD/bonus-adjusted warrant claims apply? (7) How much growth and capital is organic? (8) What is Siddhanta's binding price/closing status and project-level return evidence? Answers may improve or worsen the result; no predetermined misconduct conclusion is sought.

Model assumptions are in model_inputs.json, model_spec.md and every canonical path. **98 complete paths**, including **59 failed paths**, are retained. Historical and valuation calculations are rebuilt from declared authored inputs with no network/source dependency. Sixteen framework checks are addressed, with unresolved evidence shown rather than claiming every issuer question is closed. Standalone audit scope is never silently generalized to all subsidiaries, and a management forecast in an exchange filing remains a management forecast.
